# Ryu shortest binary64 formatting: known answers, from upstream's own suite.
#
# Provenance
#   Every expected string below is the literal upstream asserts, copied from
#   the gtest cases of `ASSERT_D2S(...)` in ryu/ryu/tests/d2s_test.cc at the
#   pinned upstream revision 4c0618b0e44f7ef027ebae05d2cc7812048f7c8f.
#   Nothing in this file was computed by this fork.  Upstream's generated
#   tables (all_powers_of_ten / all_binary_exponents) are not copied; the
#   hand-written cases upstream names one by one are.
#
# Line format
#   <input-spec> TAB <expected string>
#
#   input-spec is one of
#     zero | negzero | nan | inf | neginf
#         the five non-finite/signed cases of d2s_test.cc:37-45
#     bits   <16 hex digits>
#         upstream's int64Bits2Double(0x...) helper (d2s_test.cc:27)
#     parts  <sign 0|1> <exponent> <mantissa>
#         upstream's ieeeParts2Double(sign, exponent, mantissa)
#         (d2s_test.cc:29-33); the mantissa keeps the literal base upstream
#         wrote it in
#     lit    <decimal literal>
#         the upstream C literal, with any `f` suffix dropped
#
#   A few upstream inputs are written as a sum of two exactly representable
#   decimal literals (SmallIntegers, 10^15 + 10^i).  Each is recorded here as
#   its exact value, which parses back to the identical binary64.
#
#   Blank lines and lines beginning with `#` are ignored.
#
# The exponent marker is upstream's: uppercase `E`, no `+`, no zero padding
# (`1E0`, `5E-324`, `1.7976931348623157E308`).  That spelling is part of the
# known answer and is not normalised anywhere.
